title: Rabbi Yehudah bar Gamda of Kefar Akko

paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah bar Gamda of Kefar Akko. (A tanna.) He is mentioned in [Sotah 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.43b.12): ‘Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits [it] in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Gamda of Kefar Akko.’ The saying appears in Tosefta, Kilayim, chapter 1, in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Agra. In the Mekhilta, Yitro, Massekhta de-Amalek, chapter 2, Yehudah of Kefar Akko asked Rabban Gamliel.[^1]
We also find Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah of Kefar Akko, a student of Rabbi Shimon, in [Sotah 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.37b.5-6); see his entry.[^2]

notes.text: The prior supplied transcription’s מהיר is corrected to מתיר, ‘permits,’ from the actual native page (PDF 142, printed 559) and the named William Davidson Hebrew edition of [Sotah 43b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.43b.12). The full parallel concerns layering a tree into a vegetable plant; [it] supplies the English object without adding that context to Hyman’s abbreviated quotation. The expansions of ב״ג, ר״י ב״ג and ר״ג follow the heading and immediate attribution. Yehudah ben Agra remains a distinct source variant. The Tosefta and Mekhilta passages were not independently checked.

The prior supplied proofread text has לו: (36b), but the native page reads לז: (37b); the exact passage naming Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah of Kefar Akko in Rabbi Shimon’s name occurs in the named William Davidson edition at [Sotah 37b:5–6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.37b.5-6). The corrected locator is used in the English; the original form is retained here. תלמידו דר״ש means a student of Rabbi Shimon. The source’s כסוטה is rendered contextually as ‘in Sotah.’ No new identity binding is made.
